prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a tiered cafe layout where the camera wearer's hands and smartphone at bottom center are nearest (brightest white, ~0.3–0.4 m, within the wearer's arm's reach), immediately in front of a round black table (~0.4–0.9 m) holding upright menu stands that partially occlude the lower torsos of people behind them, and an adjacent rectangular table to the right (~0.8–1.5 m). Across frames 1–4, three seated people form a middle depth band (~1.2–1.8 m, spaced ~0.5–0.8 m apart): a woman in black on the left facing right/forward, a person in a black shirt and cap directly in front facing the wearer while looking down at a handheld phone within their reach, and a person in a white shirt and cap on the right leaning over the right table looking down toward a menu held by a partially visible person at the bottom-right edge (~0.8–1.0 m). Behind the central person stands another person in a tan shirt (~2.0–2.5 m, partially occluded), while in frame 5 the camera pans right by ~30–40 degrees, shifting the black-shirted person to the left edge and revealing two additional seated people on the right (~1.2–2.0 m) facing left toward the table. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the foreground menu stands and table surfaces from the overlapping people behind them and distinguishes the standing person's depth plane from the seated row. However, the map is unreliable on the flat tabletops where it renders a steep brightness gradient as if vertical, merges the wearer's hands and phone into a saturated white blob, and flattens the outdoor patio background (3–6+ m) into uniform black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the discrete people and small objects across the scene, identifying the camera wearer's smartphone at bottom center (~0.3–0.4 m, within arm's reach) and the handheld phone within reach of the central seated person (~1.3 m in front), alongside the main foreground group (~1.2–2.5 m) and several distant background figures (~3–5 m) at the upper left and center-right who are partly occluded by window pillars and foreground bodies. In frames 1–4, it separates the woman on the left (~1.5 m, turning her head from right to forward by frame 4), the central person facing the wearer (~1.4 m), the standing person behind them (~2.0 m), and the white-shirted person on the right (~1.4 m, facing down/right toward the person partly in view at bottom right, ~0.9 m), before the rightward camera turn in frame 5 brings two more right-side seated people (~1.2–1.8 m, facing left) into view. Unlike the RGB image where dark clothing and busy backgrounds blend together, the segmentation map makes small handheld phones and partially occluded background patrons at upper left and right immediately distinguishable as separate instances. However, the map is unreliable on furniture and tabletop items: it completely misses the round and rectangular tables and upright menu stands, misclassifies the left table and adjacent regions as 'chair' and parts of the central person's torso as part of the foreground phone or 'cup' (frame 2), and hallucinates 'potted plant' and 'bottle' labels on the white-shirted person and menu in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D body skeletons (yellow) and hand keypoints (magenta) primarily for two individuals across the strip: the central seated person in black (~1.4 m in front, facing the wearer) and the seated person in white to their right (~1.4 m away, ~0.7 m right of the central person, angled down and right). In frame 1, the central person's upper torso, thighs, and raised left hand (holding a phone at chest level within arm's reach) are tracked alongside a detached magenta hand skeleton near the bottom-left of the right table (~1.0 m), whereas in frames 2–4 the central person's body skeleton drops out (leaving only a single hand in frame 2) while the white-shirted person's forward-leaning torso, crossed arms, and right hand resting on the table (~1.2 m) are tracked. In frame 5, as the camera turns right, all torso skeletons disappear and only a single magenta hand skeleton remains near the bottom right (~0.9 m) belonging to the foreground person holding a menu on the right. Compared to RGB, the pose map clarifies the exact shoulder tilt, elbow bend, and forearm orientation of the white-shirted person leaning over the table in frames 2–4 despite foreshortening. However, the map is highly incomplete and unreliable overall, failing to detect the camera wearer's own hands at the bottom (~0.3 m), the woman on the left, the standing person behind, the right-side group in frame 5, and most lower limbs occluded beneath the tables.
